answer: In an agent economy, each seller supplying saffron to a mesa outpost must lock $100 for 30 days before its account can submit bids, with one bid slot per bond. Orders may use a cipher for privacy, but every account still needs its own bond. An attacker creating 1,000 fake sellers must immobilize $100,000 for a month; splitting accounts creates no extra bidding capacity per dollar, so identities alone confer no advantage.
